subChunks.title: Scalability & Availability Patterns

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Designing for scale means assuming failure. Any server can die at any moment. Any network call can fail. Design your system so that individual failures are isolated, not catastrophic.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Implement exponential backoff: backoffDelay(int attempt) returns baseDelay * 2^attempt milliseconds (base = 100ms). Print delays for attempts 0-3.
guidedPractice.hint: Return (long)(100 * Math.pow(2, attempt)). Loop i from 0 to 3 and print "Attempt " + i + ": " + backoffDelay(i) + "ms".

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain the CAP theorem with an example. What does a system sacrifice when choosing AP over CP?

questions.prompt: What does horizontal scaling require that vertical scaling does not?
options: Stateless application design — session state must be externalised (e.g., Redis)
questions.answer: Stateless application design — session state must be externalised (e.g., Redis)
questions.explanation: With multiple instances, any request can hit any server. Server-side session storage won't work — use an external store like Redis.

subChunks.title: Caching Strategies

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Caching is like a wizard memorising a spell they cast often — rather than looking it up in the Tome every time. The risk: if the Tome changes, the memory is wrong. TTL and cache eviction are the solution.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate cache-aside: getProduct(int id) — if id is in the cache map, print "Cache hit: " + cached value; otherwise print "Cache miss, loading: " + id and add it to cache.
guidedPractice.hint: Check cache.containsKey(id). On miss, set loaded = "Product-" + id, print the miss message, then cache.put(id, loaded).

tests.label: Cache
tests.expected:
Cache miss, loading: 1
Cache hit: Product-1
Cache miss, loading: 2

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain cache invalidation challenges. What is a cache stampede and how can you prevent it?

questions.prompt: What is a TTL (Time-to-Live) in caching?
options: The duration after which a cached entry expires and is removed
The time taken to load data into cache
The maximum cache size in megabytes
The time to live before the server restarts
questions.answer: The duration after which a cached entry expires and is removed
questions.explanation: TTL prevents stale data by auto-expiring cache entries. After TTL, the next request re-fetches from the source.

subChunks.title: Database Design & Sharding

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Indexing is the most impactful optimisation you will ever make. A table scan on 100 million rows takes minutes. A B-tree index lookup takes milliseconds. Always add indexes on foreign keys and filter columns.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate sharding: given a userId, determine shard number using userId % numShards. Print shard assignment for users 0-4 with 3 shards.
guidedPractice.hint: getShard returns userId % numShards. Loop userId from 0 to 4 and print "User " + userId + " -> Shard " + getShard(userId, 3).

tests.label: Sharding
tests.expected:
User 0 -> Shard 0
User 1 -> Shard 1
User 2 -> Shard 2
User 3 -> Shard 0
User 4 -> Shard 1

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain CQRS. What problem does it solve in high-scale systems?

questions.prompt: What is the primary purpose of a database read replica?
options: Offload read traffic from the primary, improving read scalability and write performance
Store backup data in case of primary failure
questions.answer: Offload read traffic from the primary, improving read scalability and write performance
questions.explanation: Read replicas replicate data from the primary. Routing reads to replicas reduces primary load, leaving it free for writes.

subChunks.title: Event-Driven Architecture & Message Patterns

storyBeats.speaker: Archmage Eldrin
storyBeats.text: Event Sourcing is the ultimate audit log — instead of storing the current state, you store every change that led to it. Want to know an order's history? Replay its events. Want to rebuild a corrupted read model? Replay all events from the beginning.

guidedPractice.problemHtml: Simulate event sourcing: apply a list of events to a balance. Events: "DEPOSIT:100", "DEPOSIT:50", "WITHDRAW:30". Print final balance.
guidedPractice.hint: Split each event on ":". If parts[0] is "DEPOSIT" add amount, if "WITHDRAW" subtract. Print "Final balance: " + balance.

subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain Event Sourcing. What advantage does it have over traditional state-based persistence?

questions.prompt: What problem does the Outbox Pattern solve?
options: Ensures events are published to Kafka atomically with the database transaction — no events lost if the broker is down
questions.answer: Ensures events are published to Kafka atomically with the database transaction — no events lost if the broker is down
questions.explanation: Writing to an outbox table in the same transaction as the business operation guarantees the event is eventually published, even if Kafka is temporarily unavailable.
